parsedVerdict.reasoning: AssignTaskUseCase.execute coordinates one use case. It loads a task and a user through repository interfaces from the domain layer, throws an error if either one is missing, builds an updated Task with the new assignee, and saves it through the repository abstraction. That is application-layer work. The file has no persistence code (no SQL, ORM or storage calls), no transport or HTTP handling, and no framework code. It also has no real business rule that should live in the domain layer. Copying the task's fields into a new Task with the new assignee could be moved into a domain method such as task.assignTo(userId). That would be a design improvement, not a responsibility in the wrong layer. No ADR prose was provided.
